key_insight: In porous media under ambient flow, the direction of the salt gradient determines where colloids are extracted: from the perimeter in solute-out mode and from the stagnant core in solute-in mode, with diffusioosmosis boosting both.
engineering_relevance: Tuning phoretic and osmotic transport offers a route to improve membrane filtration, laundry detergency, and enhanced oil recovery in porous structures.
method: 2D porous lattice of hexagonally packed pillars/fibers with equal spacing
Finite-element simulations of ambient-flow exposure with solute-out and solute-in gradient orientations
Compared colloidal extraction patterns with and without diffusioosmotic slip on internal surfaces
evidence_signal: Finite-element results in the abstract show qualitatively different extraction patterns for the two gradient orientations, with stronger diffusioosmotic enhancement in solute-in mode.
watch_item: The findings come from simulation of an idealized 2D porous lattice, so performance in irregular 3D media and real fluids may differ.
paper_title: Colloid recovery from porous structures under ambient flow: enhanced extraction via phoretic and osmotic mechanisms
